results.tiebreak:
Val is a crop of the same capture, about 1.75x tighter. After a single near-isotropic affine (SIFT/RANSAC, then ECC 0.97 at train resolution), the man's head tilt, both gloved hands, the wristwatch, the chainsaw bar angle and the dangling chain on the log all land on the same spots. Per-patch phase correlation leaves residual shifts of about 1 px or less, noisy, with no subject-vs-background offset, so nothing shows him moving between two burst frames. The skeptic's 'different chainsaw pose' is a misreading: the waist-level bar is identical in both, and the lower horizontal bar in train is simply outside val's frame. Two caveats: val is more saturated, and a thin strip on its left (a yellow-clad bystander) falls just outside train's frame, so train itself was likely cropped from a larger original. results.tiebreak: Val is the train photo mirrored, scaled about 1.2x and cropped, with a 'La Quinta Rentals' logo pasted on and the sky brightened. results.tiebreak: These are the same ball and the same patch of green: after alignment the dimple pattern and individual grass blades line up, and the ball silhouette sits within 1 px with no parallax. But the frames are two different exposures. Train is a full 2:3 portrait frame and val a full 3:2 landscape frame, related by a consistent ~4.5 deg tilt and ~0.93 scale (RANSAC across thresholds). Each also shows what the other lacks: train has about 100 px (val scale) more foreground grass below the ball, and val has more grass to the right. So neither can be a crop of the other, and this looks like a vertical/horizontal pair shot from one setup, not one image resold under two watermarks.

results.tiebreak: A single scale+shift (similarity) transform lines the yellow saw up with the red one at sub-pixel accuracy: 29 SIFT inliers spread across the front handle, the bottom of the handguard and the rear knobs/handle, mean residual 0.7 px. After alignment the outlines of the bar, handguard, top cover and rear handle overlap, and small details sit in the same spots on both (the side vents, the clutch-cover holes, the two rear knobs, even the small hole near the bar tip). The yellow version is a soft, washed-out retouch: the top-cover facets are flattened, the chain looks painted, there is a Vigor decal on the bar and the background is white. So the "different cover shape and controls" the skeptic saw are retouching and blur, not a different pose or product. This is one studio photo, recolored and edited.
